headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network access create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; compliance gaps are plausible but undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise reads and writes server filesystem files and can ingest uploaded files; the course agent also reads/writes files and uses stdin/stdout plus API endpoints. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let one agent’s content be treated as instructions by the other. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or uploaded-file store
IF agent_b parses file or API content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported files
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs, model provider keys, and tool credentials while having broad network egress; the course agent handles academic papers plus configuration secrets and can write files. If they share a workspace or credentials path, sensitive data can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or outbound requests. The interaction is not directly evidenced, so I choose high over medium due to the sensitive data classes.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same secrets file or mounted volume
IF either agent forwards file contents to external model providers or APIs
mitigations: Restrict outbound domains for both agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, and Flowise explicitly supports shared state via server datastore while the course agent runs in a local development environment with Docker Compose. Concurrent writes to overlapping paths or shared state can corrupt artifacts or overwrite each other. Because locking is not stated, the safer choice is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem tree or datastore
IF concurrent runs occur without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer per shared resource
Add file locks around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder, so its outputs can become downstream inputs; the course agent exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints and can act on retrieved content. If the course agent treats Flowise-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or published content. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is risky by default.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without an explicit verification step
IF agent_a-generated text is used to drive API calls or published responses
mitigations: Log and diff all inter-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff payloads

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and tool credentials, while the course agent touches academic papers, metadata, research questions, and configuration secrets. The profiles do not state residency or certification mismatches, so I cannot claim a breach. However, differing secret-handling and retention expectations create a plausible compliance gap if the same regulated data class is routed through both.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through both agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across deployments
